Launch the Interactive Walkability Application

Source: R/app.R
walk_app.Rd

Launches an interactive web application built with Shiny, bslib, and mapgl (MapLibre GL JS) for visual exploration and quantitative analysis of urban street networks.

Usage

walk_app(
  network = NULL,
  host = "127.0.0.1",
  port = NULL,
  launch.browser = TRUE,
  lang = c("es", "en"),
  ...
)

Arguments

network

Optional initial walk_network object. If NULL (default), the app allows selecting among the built-in model cities (Cusco, Lima, Arequipa) or uploading a custom street dataset.

host

Character. The IPv4 address that the application should listen on (default "127.0.0.1").

port

Integer. The TCP port that the application should listen on. Default is randomly selected.

launch.browser

Logical. Whether to open the application in the system's default browser (default TRUE).

lang

Character string specifying the initial interface language: "es" for Spanish (default) or "en" for English. The user can also toggle the language interactively at runtime via the navbar selector.

...

Additional arguments passed to shiny::runApp().

Value

Runs the Shiny application (returns invisible NULL).

Details

The application provides dedicated, fully documented workspaces for:

  • Pedestrian Reachability (10-min Reach): Spatial gradient of walkable network length with partial-edge credits in Rust.

  • Multi-Threshold Isochrones: Concentric, non-overlapping topological rings (e.g. 5, 10, 15 min) or cumulative hulls.

  • Point-to-Point Routing & Circuity: Optimal shortest path, travel time, and detour ratio.

  • Network Morphology & Intersection Density: Topological node valence classification (cul-de-sacs, 3-way, 4-way+).

  • Scenario Simulation: Testing street closures and pedestrianization with before/after comparison.

  • Documentation & Code Generator: Detailed methodology and reproducible R scripts.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
# Launch with default language (Spanish):
walk_app()

# Launch in English:
walk_app(lang = "en")

# Launch with a pre-built network:
utils::data(streets_cusco)
net <- walk_build_network(streets_cusco, verbose = FALSE)
walk_app(net, lang = "es")
}
